- When sentiment is high (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for high sentiment periods.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon, especially after price spikes; apply a 2–5 day lag correction for the first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 2–4% per day until convergence.
- Sentiment drops below 0.25 for 3+ consecutive days → model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for bearish sentiment decay.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is low and price is trending down; adjust downward bias by +1–2% for low sentiment + falling price patterns.
